conf.description: Cisco Duo MFA telephony (v2) / syslog-cef (DuoLogSync): hand-built CEF decode - no stock cisco_duo CEF pipeline exists - splits the header, extracts cs1..cs5 (cs1's context value can contain spaces so it gets a lookahead capture), resolves each by its cs#Label, casts credits to numeric, hashes the phone-number PII, and leaves rt-derived _time unset on v2 tenants where DLS emits the literal 'None'.

conf.comment: cisco-duo / telephony / syslog-cef. DLS's telephony CEF mapping reads a 'timestamp' key into rt, but the v2 record's time field is 'ts' (ISO8601) with no 'timestamp' key, so rt is the literal string 'None' on a v2 tenant and CEF carries no other time field - _time is only set when rt parses as a real number; on 'None' it is left unset (documented gap, not fabricated). cs1..cs5 are resolved by matching each cs#Label ('context','credits','event_type','phone','type'), not by slot position. phone_number is hashed (C.Mask.md5) rather than truncated to country+area code, since no country-calling-code length table is supplied in this work order - hashing is the one PII option that needs no invented table. CEF omits telephony_id/txid entirely, so no join key back to the auth log survives this format. Order: header split -> extension extract -> eval (from ORIGINAL names) -> rename -> mask.

functions.description: the v2 rt='None' gap, label-not-slot rule, and why hashing was chosen over country-code truncation
split the fixed CEF:0|Duo Security|DuoLogSync|<ver>|<eventtype>|<eventtype>|5| header from the extension

extract each known CEF extension key independently (order-independent); cs1 alone gets a lookahead-terminated capture since the context value ('Administrator Login', 'Authentication') can contain spaces

resolve cs1..cs5 by label into the five telephony custom fields, cast credits to numeric, convert rt when it is a real number (v2 tenants emit the literal string 'None', left unset rather than fabricated) - all from ORIGINAL field names before rename

batch rename the header fields that need no further transform; every telephony value field is custom-namespaced (no ECS field models an out-of-band delivery channel or telephony credits) and was already written directly by the eval above

hash the resolved phone number - subscriber PII in E.164 form - per recommendations.direct.cribl's 'hash the subscriber digits' option; no country-calling-code length table is supplied to implement the alternative truncate-to-country-code option
hash the same phone-number text where it still sits verbatim in _raw, so the unmasked digits do not leak downstream via the raw copy
